findings.title: Async legacy write inherits cancelled request context
findings.body: Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection all do `go func() { ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx,...)` where `ctx` is the request-scoped context. Once the handler returns the parent context is cancelled, so the 10s timeout child is immediately cancelled and the legacy write is aborted. The consequence is mode 3 silently never mirrors to legacy, defeating its safety purpose. Use a detached context e.g. `context.WithoutCancel` / `context.Background()` plus timeout and copy of logger/values.

findings.title: Reusing UpdatedObjectInfo concurrently in background goroutine
findings.body: Update calls `d.Storage.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` synchronously and then passes the same `objInfo` to `d.Legacy.Update` in a `go` routine. `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo.UpdatedObject()` is generally single-use and not safe for concurrent/repeated evaluation, and the previous implementation deliberately wrapped the already-computed `updated` object in an `updateWrapper`. Re-invoking it for legacy can return a different object, fail, or race, causing legacy/storage divergence.

findings.title: Legacy Create uses pre-storage input object instead of created result
findings.body: Create writes `created` back to the caller but asynchronously writes the original input `obj` to legacy. Any defaults, UIDs, resourceVersions or mutations applied by unified storage are lost in legacy, guaranteeing permanent divergence between the two stores. The legacy call should use the `created` object snapshot.

findings.title: Storage Create failure recorded as legacy duration
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, Create calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with `startStorage`. The same copy-paste error exists on the Update storage-error path at line 129. This misattributes storage latency/errors to legacy metrics, hiding storage outages and breaking dashboards/alerts keyed on mode/kind/method.

findings.title: Delete records object name in kind label
findings.body: On successful storage Delete the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, ...)` passing the object `name` where every other call passes `options.Kind`. This creates unbounded high-cardinality metric label values (one series per object name) and makes delete latency unqueryable by kind.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection recorded as storage duration
findings.body: The background legacy DeleteCollection path calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy delete-collection latency/errors will never appear under the legacy metric and will pollute storage metrics.

findings.title: Delete drops enriched logger context
findings.body: Delete builds `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", ..., "method", ...)` but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of using `log` like Create/Update/DeleteCollection do. Request-scoped logs and the background legacy delete lose name/kind/method fields, hindering debugging.
